concepts.name: Validated Learning
concepts.description: Startups create value by rapidly learning what customers truly want, not by building products. By focusing on experiments that generate data, founders avoid building wasteful features and instead validate assumptions about business sustainability.

concepts.name: Small Batches / Just‑in‑Time Experiments
concepts.description: Using the lean manufacturing principle of single‑piece flow, startups conduct experiments in tiny batches. This reduces inventory, exposes defects early, and allows quicker iteration without large upfront planning.

concepts.name: Growth Engine Focus
concepts.description: Sustainable growth follows one of three engines—paid, viral, or sticky. By identifying the dominant engine, a startup directs resources to the most effective metrics and experiments.

concepts.name: Lean Organizational Design
concepts.description: Traditional departmental incentives are replaced by lean structures that foster collaboration and keep teams nimble. A balance of minimal process and empowerment prevents bureaucratic slow‑downs while scaling.

concepts.name: Innovation Accounting
concepts.description: Innovation accounting turns learning outcomes into measurable metrics. It helps founders detect when growth risks stall and decide to pivot or persevere.

concepts.name: Continuous Improvement Tools
concepts.description: Techniques like the Five Whys help teams investigate problems quickly, avoiding bureaucracy and maintaining functional health during growth.

concepts.name: Scaling While Maintaining DNA
concepts.description: Even as a startup matures, a lean foundation allows it to grow into a lean enterprise that retains its speed, learning orientation, and culture of innovation.

concepts.name: Portfolio Management of Innovation
concepts.description: Established companies must manage both incremental and disruptive projects simultaneously. Incubating innovation teams inside the enterprise keeps the entrepreneurial spirit alive.

concepts.name: Waste Not Culture
concepts.description: The Lean Startup movement encourages continual waste elimination, learning from past industrial movements, and setting a future path for ongoing improvement.
